rules.statement: Encrypt every persisted private or symmetric key value (signing keys, encryption keys, client secrets) as an envelope under the secret protection key hierarchy; store only public material (SPKI, X.509 certificates) unencrypted.
rules.why: A database dump or backup should not expose any secret without the external root key, and a key ring stored beside the data only moves the problem.
rules.check: Look for new stored fields or encodings holding private or symmetric key material, or secrets, that are written as plaintext or protected by anything other than the envelope protector; any encoding other than public `spki`/`x509` must be an envelope.

rules.statement: When encrypting a stored value, bind the ciphertext through AEAD associated data to its owner, purpose and item id. Normalize case-insensitive identifiers with `ToLowerInvariant` the same way the store does, and compare purposes ordinally.
rules.why: Binding stops a value moved to another row, tenant or purpose from decrypting, and the binding has to match the store's own identifier normalization.
rules.check: Flag protect or unprotect calls that leave out associated data or leave out owner, purpose or item id. Also flag binding code that normalizes identifiers inconsistently (culture-sensitive casing, or no lower-casing when the store lower-cases) or compares purposes with a non-ordinal comparison.

rules.statement: Draw a fresh random 256-bit data key for each protect operation, encrypt the value with AES-256-GCM, and wrap the data key with a purpose key that is derived with HKDF-SHA256 from the master key and never stored.
rules.why: Envelope encryption with per-record data keys and derived purpose keys means rotating a master key only rewraps small data keys, with no extra stored per-purpose state.
rules.check: Look for reuse of a data key across records, ciphers other than AES-256-GCM for envelopes, or purpose keys being persisted instead of derived with HKDF.

rules.statement: When wrapping a master key with an external KMS or HSM root key, bind the owner and key id as associated data (the KMS encryption context) wherever the service supports it.
rules.why: The root key provider only wraps and unwraps master keys, and binding owner and key id stops a wrapped key from being unwrapped for a different owner.
rules.check: Check that root key provider implementations pass owner and key id as encryption context or associated data when the service supports it.

rules.statement: Do the asynchronous step of loading or creating key material (which may call a remote KMS) once, through an async acquisition method, and make the returned protector do its cryptography synchronously.
rules.why: Only loading master keys may reach the key management service, so the hot cryptographic path stays synchronous.
rules.check: Flag protector APIs that make encrypt/decrypt async or call the KMS during them, and acquisition paths that block synchronously on KMS calls.

rules.statement: Acquire a secret protector, or any resource that lazily creates per-owner key material, only after the request is authorized and validated and the target secret is known to exist.
rules.why: Acquiring early would let a request that names an unknown owner create a master key.
rules.check: Look for protector or key-material acquisition calls placed before authorization checks, before input validation, or before confirming the secret or owner exists.

rules.statement: In cryptographic and secret-handling code, write output into caller-supplied writers or spans and put a sizing method beside each producer, rent transient buffers, keep secrets in pinned buffers that are zeroed on release, and never hold sensitive text in a `string`.
rules.why: A `string` or an unpinned, unzeroed buffer cannot be wiped, so secret bytes stay in managed memory.
rules.check: Flag secrets returned as `string` or `byte[]`, `new byte[]` used for transient buffers, secret buffers that are not pinned or not cleared on dispose, and producers with no matching size method.

rules.statement: Create a `string` only for a non-secret value at a storage or wire boundary (such as an envelope in a text column, a wrapped key, or a KMS encryption context), and write it once, in place, with `string.Create`.
rules.why: Building the string once in place avoids intermediate allocations, and keeping strings at the boundary keeps secrets out of immutable managed text.
rules.check: Flag string concatenation, StringBuilder or intermediate `ToString` calls used to build envelope or encoded key text, and any string that holds secret material.

rules.statement: Keep envelope formats, master key handling, key derivation and root key wrappers internal; expose only the protector abstraction to applications and other packages.
rules.why: Keeping these internal lets them evolve (for example, master key rotation) without breaking consumers.
rules.check: Flag new public types or members that expose envelope layout, master keys, derivation details or root wrapper implementations.

rules.statement: Use a namespaced `<vendor>/<name>` purpose string when protecting application or package data through a shared secret protector.
rules.why: Namespaced purposes keep each consumer's keys separate, while every consumer still gets the root key, tenant isolation and binding.
rules.check: Flag protector calls in consuming code that pass a purpose string without a vendor namespace prefix.

rules.statement: Never commit a root key or other key-encryption key to the repository, not even one for development; generate development keys per machine outside the repository, or use an ephemeral key.
rules.why: A committed root key is a leaked key.
rules.check: Look for key files, base64 key values or inline key configuration added to the repository, including appsettings.Development files.

rules.statement: Have Production startup refuse ephemeral key providers, inline key material in configuration (even when that provider is not selected), and an undecided recovery setting, and report these together with every other production-safety finding instead of failing on the first one.
rules.why: An unused root key in configuration is still a leaked key, and losing the root key with no recovery key loses every stored secret.
rules.check: Check that production safety validation covers new key or secret options, rejects inline keys and ephemeral providers, and collects findings instead of throwing on the first one.

rules.statement: When caching unwrapped keys, do not cache a load that an eviction overtook, and do not zero a key on eviction; zero cached key memory only when the owning cache or ring is disposed.
rules.why: A protector handed out earlier may still be using an evicted key, and caching a load that raced an eviction would bring back stale keys.
rules.check: Look for cache eviction code that clears key buffers, and for load-then-store code that does not check whether an eviction happened during the load.
